checksums.name: generic_stamp_sum16_xor16 (unmapped candidate)
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_0801b8c0 builds a 12-byte stamp: 6-byte literal magic + u16 version(0x0100) + u16 additive signed-word sum over 500 bytes (FUN_0801b958) + u16 XOR-word checksum over the same 500 bytes (FUN_0801b980). FUN_0801b914 verifies only the magic+version, never the sum16/xor16 fields. No byte-offset alignment of this 12-byte struct against the observed 16-byte header was found to be consistent (see report section 4.4).

checksums.name: header_bytes_0B_0D_0F (candidate counters, unresolved algorithm)
checksums.formula_detail: Single bytes at offsets 0x0B, 0x0D, 0x0F each increase by +5 between cap-00 and cap-01 while interleaved bytes 0x0C (0x15) and 0x0E (0x60) stay constant. sum8/xor8/sum16/xor16 over every tested byte window (0x00-0x1FF, multiple start/length combinations) failed to reproduce these deltas non-trivially; see report section 4.3 for the exact Python verification performed.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer primitive: programs src/dst/count|enable globals, busy-polls completion bit, used for both EEPROM read and write bit-streams
EEPROM READ command builder + DMA3 bit-serialize (2-bit opcode '11' + 6-bit record address) and 64-bit response unpack into 4x u16 words; MMIO seed function
EEPROM WRITE command builder + DMA3 bit-serialize (2-bit opcode '10' + 6-bit address + 64-bit payload), busy-polls 0x0D000000 ready bit; MMIO seed function
Write-verify: reads back via FUN_08024584 and compares against expected 4x u16 words, returns 0x8000 on mismatch
Top of hardware tier: write-with-retry orchestrator, up to 3 attempts of write(FUN_08024634)+verify(FUN_08024710); no static caller found in callgraph.json
Arms a secondary transfer descriptor / enable flag immediately before the EEPROM busy-poll in the write path
Disarms/tears down the descriptor armed by FUN_08024438
Generic interrupt-vector get/set dispatch (mode selector 4/0x40/other), used to install a transfer-complete callback
Generic record-count/metadata setter (bounds-checked against 4), used during per-transfer setup

open_questions: What algorithm (if any) produces the three single-byte values at offsets 0x0B, 0x0D, 0x0F, which moved by an identical +5 delta between the two captured snapshots?
Which game-logic function(s) outside the provided 111-function decompilation window populate and consume the 50-entry record table at offset 0x18-0x1A7?

Is the generic FUN_0801b8c0/FUN_0801b914 magic+version+sum16+xor16 stamp pair actually responsible for any bytes in this specific 512-byte save, given that no offset alignment in [0,16) reproduces its expected 12-byte shape?

What is the scheduling/trigger mechanism (indirect task-table call) that invokes FUN_0801b518 (read task) and FUN_0801b684 (write task), since neither has a statically-recorded caller in callgraph.json?

Is the first record at offset 0x10-0x17 (trailing bytes 01 01 01 00, non-ASCII) a config/options record distinct from the following 50 score-table entries, or is it a writer-side artifact of a shared record-initialization routine?

What determines the true per-block record count (the data shows irregular block boundaries at 9-10-10-9-11 entries), and is the all-zero final record at 0x1A0 a genuine terminator or simply an unused slot?
